answer: A reputation-weighted stake is the inlet through which new agents enter the economy: each identity must lock a deposit that grows with the trust it earns, so a sybil swarm cannot simply clone itself for free. Like a comet burning off mass on every pass, each fake identity pays real fees for attestations, compute, and slashing risk, while honest work slowly compounds reputation. When a gale of cheap clones hits, the cost curve stays linear for the attacker but the reward stays capped by stake-weighted voting, so flooding the network costs more than it can ever extract.
